was: Municipal campground owned and managed by the City of Soap Lake on the SW shore of Soap Lake; RV sites with full hookups plus a lakefront beach/park; reservable online (Campspot). Serves overnight through long-term guests. --Claude
note: City of Soap Lake campground on the lake, owned and managed by the city, with a camp host.  It has 22 lakefront and 6 back-side RV sites and 15 primitive tent sites. --Claude

was: Small country inn + RV park on Hwy 26 in Dayville, John Day River valley, ~9 mi from the Sheep Rock Unit of John Day Fossil Beds NM. 15 full-hookup RV sites on grassy back-in spots with picnic tables; large clean shower house; also inn rooms and a few tent sites. Reservable online. --Claude
note: Country inn and RV park in Dayville, in a craftsman house built in 1908 for the mill owner Walt Greenwell and converted into an inn in 1991, nine miles from the Sheep Rock Unit of the John Day Fossil Beds and the Thomas Condon Paleontology Center.  The seven full-hookup spaces behind the inn are each 60 ft long on level gravel, separated by grass and trees, and the five power-only sites are on the lawn and have picnic tables.  Guests share a community fire pit with a bar and grill, barbecue grills and horseshoe pits; the John Day River, the town park and playground, the Dayville Cafe, the Mercantile and the South Fork Mini Market & Gas are within walking distance, and there are swimming holes nearby.  EV charging costs $10 an hour or $30 a day, and an RV check-in before 2 p.m. costs $10; monthly winter rates, November through April, are by phone.  The inn also has rooms and an Airstream Bambi for glamping. --Claude

was: Private resort on 16 acres near Frenchglen, ~3 mi SE of Hwy 205 on the Steens Mtn North Loop Rd, overlooking the Donner und Blitzen River valley and Malheur NWR. 78 sites — full hookups plus electric / electric-water sites, 30/50 amp — plus tent sites and cabins; general store, laundry, wifi, restrooms. Seasonal office (Apr 16–Oct 10 main season). Transient, reservable online. --Claude
note: High-desert resort on 16 acres at Frenchglen, surrounded by the Malheur National Wildlife Refuge and its marshes; it has 38 RV sites, 14 grass-and-shade tent sites and seven lodging options, from cabins to the two-bedroom Homestead.  EV charging is offered only at site 39, by advance reservation.  A two-night minimum applies over Memorial Day weekend, the 4th of July, the Steens Rim Run, the Frenchglen Jamboree and Labor Day weekend.  Frenchglen's small mercantile, gas station and restaurant are typically open from mid-March through October.  Cell service is limited, and the Wi-Fi is meant for email and browsing, not streaming; mosquitoes can be prevalent in late spring and early summer. --Claude

was: Newer big-rig pull-through RV resort at 7350 New Hope Rd (Murphy, SW of Grants Pass) on the Applegate River, alongside a 9-hole golf course. 24 spacious pull-through sites with 30/50 amp electric + water hookups, wifi, extra-wide lanes; ADA-accessible. Transient ($35–80/night). --Claude
note: RV park and 9-hole golf course near Grants Pass, beside the Applegate River.  It has 12 sites the resort calls waterfront and 12 standard sites, on wide paved lanes.  The clubhouse has a full bar, snacks and a patio, and there are a pro shop, a golf simulator and a snack bar; weddings are held under a wisteria-covered gazebo.  RV guests can add golf for $25 for two people all day, cart not included, and stays are limited to 29 days. --Claude

was: Commercial park on the Rogue River east of Grants Pass (8880 Rogue River Hwy); 40 full-hookup sites incl premium riverfront, concrete pads, pull-thrus for big rigs, WiFi/laundry/showers; nightly/weekly/monthly, reservable online. --Claude
note: RV resort on 400 ft of Rogue River frontage, minutes from downtown Grants Pass, on historic grounds with mature trees, a clubhouse and pool table, gardens, a pond and a dog park.  Its premium riverfront sites, big-rig pull-throughs and shaded back-ins all have concrete pads and cable TV, and there are three family restrooms.  Guests can reach the river directly for fishing and wading, and the public boat launch at John F. Fleming Memorial Park is a block away.  Aggressive breeds such as Pit Bulls and Rottweilers are not accepted. --Claude

was: Tillamook County-operated 160-acre coastal campground at 8000 Cedar Ave, Rockaway Beach, ~1.5 mi N of Garibaldi on US-101 by the north jetty of Tillamook Bay. 73 full-hookup RV sites plus 266 tent sites (under the trees) and cabins; year-round; jetty/beach access, fishing, crabbing. Reservable online (Campspot) or by phone, up to 6 months ahead. Government-run county park -> reclassified local, not private. --Claude

was: Transient RV park at the Green Valley Grocery on US-93 at Ash Springs/Hiko; ~19 sites, full hookups 30/50 amp, water/sewer, WiFi, some pull-throughs, many sites with picnic table and fire pit; accommodates rigs 26-67 ft. On-site grocery/c-store. Reservable online. --Claude
note: The Green Valley Grocery's RV park on US 93, the Great Basin Highway, at Ash Springs in Lincoln County, a stop on the way to the Extraterrestrial Highway; many sites have a picnic table and fire pit, and the whole park has striking mountain views. --Claude

was: Veteran-owned RV park at 412 N Columbia Ave in the Goldfield historic district; medium/premium back-in and extra-large pull-through sites with water, sewer and 30/50-amp electric, Wi-Fi, restrooms/showers, outdoor kitchen and common fire-pit area. Reservable online. --Claude
note: RV park in the center of Goldfield's historic district, within easy walking distance of local businesses, halfway between Reno and Las Vegas.  Goldfield, once the largest town in Nevada, boomed to 20,000 people after gold was found in 1902; it is now an art community and home to the International Car Forest and the Saint Barbara Grotto.  Bikes can be rented. --Claude

was: Pinal County Open Space & Trails park near Stanfield, ~1 mi off I-8 in the Sonoran Desert. ~19-24 gravel pull-through dry-camping sites (no hookups) accommodating rigs to 50 ft, each with a shaded ramada; vault/porta-toilets, no water/electric. $10/night, reserve online via Campspot. --Claude
note: Pinal County Open Space & Trails park near Stanfield, ~1 mi off I-8 in the Sonoran Desert. ~19-24 gravel pull-through dry-camping sites (no hookups) accommodating rigs to 50 ft, each with a shaded ramada; vault/porta-toilets, no water/electric. $10/night, reserve online via Campspot. --Claude

was: Privately owned (DECA Ranch / Duncan family, since 2023) equestrian and events center on 130 acres in Buckeye; 100+ full-hookup RV sites (30/50-amp + sewer, RVs to ~60 ft), restrooms/showers, open to all overnighters and bookable nightly via Campspot though oriented to horse and event guests. --Claude
note: Equestrian and events center in Buckeye that hosts rodeos, barrel races, roping and cutting events and weddings; it has horse stalls and The Tack Room restaurant on site, and besides its full-hookup RV park it has event sites with water and electric.  Reservations made more than 30 days ahead are subject to change. --Claude

was: Small drive-in RV park a couple miles from downtown Douglas, adjacent to Douglas Golf Course with Chiricahua Mtn backdrop. All full-hookup 30/50-amp sites, mix of pull-through and back-in, large sites; newly renovated bathhouse/laundry, pet friendly. Accepts nightly stays (~$30/night) as well as monthly; not age-restricted; reservable online via Campspot. --Claude
note: RV park in Rancho Perilla Estates, through the wrought-iron gates off AZ 80 in Douglas, next to the golf course.  Showers are paid hot showers, and there are washers and dryers.  Electric vehicles, and RVs with large solar battery packs, pay $0.18 per kWh or an extra flat $40 a night; each site takes two vehicles besides the RV, with overflow parking at $20 a month, and group sites are available.  Dogs over 50 lb are subject to approval.  The park also has Boxabl casitas, and the golf course is good for birding. --Claude

was: In-town RV park along US-60 in Springerville, White Mountains (aka Avery's RV Park, at Avery's BBQ). Full hookups with 30/50-amp long pull-throughs that fit large rigs (a reviewer parked a 36-ft Class A with room to spare); ~34 sites. Transient nightly camping, reservable online. --Claude
note: Avery's RV Park, on the main highway through Springerville beside a gas station, a convenience store, a BBQ restaurant and a bar and music venue with a party garden, within reach of mountain ranges, hiking trails and fishing lakes. --Claude

was: Newer all-ages RV resort in Sierra Vista (405 S Garden Ave) near the Huachuca Mountains; ~100-127 full-hookup (30/50-amp) concrete-pad sites including big-rig pull-throughs (rigs to 55 ft), pool, laundry, store. Transient nightly plus monthly; reservable online via Campspot. --Claude
note: Dwell Outdoor Hospitality resort in Sierra Vista at the base of the Huachuca Mountains; its back-in sites are 55 to 65 ft long and 30 ft wide.  It has a dog park, a pet wash and private bathrooms with showers.  Open flames are allowed only at the sites with fire rings, and wood fires not at all; RVs must be RVIA approved.  The deposit is the whole reservation, and a cancellation costs $20. --Claude

was: SMUD-run recreational area on 160-acre Rancho Seco Lake, Central Valley ~25 mi S of Sacramento. 21 drive-in RV sites (electric, BBQ, table, fire pit) along the SW lake rim plus ~32 tent sites; dump station, showers, boathouse; reservable, day/overnight, entry gate opens 7am. --Claude
note: SMUD's 400-acre park around a 160-acre lake fed by the Folsom South Canal, 25 miles from downtown Sacramento, with 21 RV and 32 tent sites and a designated swimming beach.  Weekend stays take two nights, Friday and Saturday together; stays are limited to 14 days, and campers with reservations cannot enter after 10 p.m.  Boat trailers have been banned since March 14, 2025 to keep out the invasive golden mussel, and hand-launched craft are inspected on entry; boats are rented on weekends and holidays from Memorial Day to Labor Day.  The lake holds bass (catch and release only), bluegill, redear sunfish and crappie, and rainbow trout are stocked from November through March.  The Howard Ranch Trail is an easy seven-mile round trip across a working cattle ranch, so dogs stay home.  The park also rents Jupes, and outside firewood is not allowed. --Claude

was: Small private RV park at 5084 Pentz Rd, Paradise, in the Sierra foothills. 43 short- and long-term sites with full hookups (20/30/50 amp), clean restrooms, hot showers; takes transient/short-term guests (bookable via Campspot). --Claude
note: RV park among tall pines in Paradise, with gravel and asphalt pads on paved roads, back-in and pull-through sites and an on-site manager; it also has 16 storage spaces.  RVs must be no more than 20 years old (management may make exceptions); generators and open fires are not allowed, dogs may weigh no more than 40 lb, and a second pet costs $25 per stay.  Stays over 10 nights are arranged by phone or online application, at $550 to $650 a month.  The office is closed on Sundays. --Claude

was: Roots/Daiva RV Resorts park on 25+ acres along the Rocky Saugeen River, 5 km north of Durham off Hwy 6. 130 sites — 67 full-hookup and 57 hydro/water on 15/30 amp — accepting RVs to 40 ft; seasonal sites plus nightly camping and a few cabins. Heated pool, playground, horseshoes/shuffleboard, laundry, store, dump station, forest walking trails. Open Apr 1 to Oct 31; nightly rates posted from about $60 CAD. Bookable online. --Claude
note: Daiva RV Resorts park beside 2,500 ft of the Rocky Saugeen River, on more than 25 acres, over 19 of them left natural with walking trails.  The river drops 30 ft over a hydro-electric dam: upstream is deep enough for swimming, diving, boating and fishing, and downstream suits nature hikes and fly-fishing.  It has a heated pool, a playground and a comfort station, horseshoe pits, shuffleboard courts and badminton and volleyball nets, and planned activities such as Christmas in July, movie nights, children's crafts, horseshoe and euchre tournaments and dances.  It also has seasonal sites and a cabin. --Claude

was: Resort on 50 acres of White Lake shoreline at 467 Bayview Lodge Rd, about 60 km west of Ottawa. Roughly 100 large drive-through RV sites, each with individually metered 30-amp hydro, water, sewer and a fire pit; short-term (nightly) camping is offered year-round alongside a seasonal program running May 7 to Oct 15. Short-term campers must have a self-contained trailer — no tents or tent trailers. Sandy beach, saltwater pool, boat rentals, store, playground, bingo hall, plus 12 cottages and 2 chalets. Reservable online. --Claude
note: Resort on 50 acres of White Lake lakefront, about 60 km west of Ottawa between Calabogie and Arnprior.  Each RV site is individually metered and has a fire pit, and sites range from full sun to full shade.  No tents; the campground page asks for trailers with washrooms.  It has a marina with gas at the docks, boat slips, boat rentals and boat storage, a saltwater pool, a recreation and games hall, a coffee shop, a fish-cleaning station and firewood.  White Lake hosts several bass tournaments a year and holds largemouth and smallmouth bass, northern pike, walleye, rock bass, yellow perch, pumpkinseed, brown bullhead and bluegill.  Cottages and chalets are also rented. --Claude

was: Small private campground on 42 wooded acres at 7140 Egremont Rd in Warwick, just east of Watford and about 30 min from Grand Bend. 15 drive-in sites with 30/15-amp power set around a small on-site pond, plus unserviced/off-grid sites; washrooms and showers, forest trails, stream, paddling on the pond. No dump station on the property. Sites are one-family (max 6 people) and bookable nightly online, with a weekly discount for 7+ nights. --Claude
note: Small family-owned campground on 42 acres of mostly natural forest in the Village of Warwick, Lambton County, with over 2 km of trails and a new dog park.  The camping area sits beside a 2-acre spring-fed lake, where motorized boats are not allowed, fishing is catch-and-release and there is no lifeguard.  Besides its powered sites it has off-grid sites, and each site takes one family with at most 2 adults and 2 pets.  Bottled drinking water and firewood are sold.  The name comes from the creek through the property, not from bears. --Claude

was: Large woodland resort beside the Grand River north of Grand Valley. Predominantly seasonal (293 full-season sites) but carries a real transient inventory of 14 overnight RV sites plus 5 overnight tent sites and 2 rental units; 294 sites with electric/water/sewer and 13 with electric/water, 30 amp maximum, sites accepting rigs to 45 ft; heated pool, comfort station, laundry, playground. Open May 1 - Oct 31, nightly rates CAD $50-80, booked online through Campspot. Chain rebranded from Harmony Resorts to Daiva RV Resorts. --Claude
note: Daiva RV Resorts park in woodland beside the Grand River, amid hundreds of acres of farmland, where mature cedars and maples surround each site and the shallow river is good for floating.  A heated pool sits in the center of the park, beside a playground and a picnic area.  The Grand Valley Trail and the Upper Grand Trailway, an old CPR line, are nearby, and the Luther Marsh Conservation Area down the street is one of Ontario's best bird-watching spots.  It also has seasonal and 11-month extended-season sites (park-model cottages with year-round access) and cabins. --Claude

was: Resort on the north shore of Stoney Lake in the Kawarthas, across the road from Petroglyphs Provincial Park. Heavily seasonal (80 full-season RV sites) but keeps a bookable transient inventory of 10 overnight RV sites plus 16 overnight tent sites and 13 wilderness sites; 90 sites with electric + water, 30 amp maximum, 16 unserviced; private sand beach, boat launch and docks, pump-out station, watercraft rentals. Open May 1 - Oct 31, nightly rates CAD $50-85 via Campspot. Chain rebranded from Harmony Resorts to Daiva RV Resorts. --Claude
note: Daiva RV Resorts park among Precambrian rock and windswept pines on the shores of Stoney Lake in the Kawarthas, with pinery and lakeside sites.  It has a private sandy beach, boat docks and a launch, and canoe and kayak rentals for exploring the lake's hundreds of islands; the lake holds bass, walleye and muskie.  Petroglyphs Provincial Park, across the street, is a sacred Indigenous site holding the largest known concentration of rock carvings in Canada, along with hiking trails and McGinnis Lake, one of the few meromictic lakes in North America.  It also has seasonal sites and boat slips. --Claude

was: Summerhill Resorts campground at 1854 County Rd 18 in Prince Edward County, on the strip between the Outlet River and the Lake Ontario dune beach at Sandbanks Provincial Park. The operator site map legend separates Full Service 50-amp and Full Service 30-amp sites (the large 100-151, 200-, 300- and 400-series rows) from a Seasonal block, plus natural tent sites, cottages and log cabins, so there is substantial nightly RV inventory; boat, kayak, canoe and paddleboard rentals and five docks on the Outlet River, beach path across Rd 18 to the lake. Nightly booking through Campspot; seasonal/annual sites also sold. --Claude
note: Summerhill Resorts campground between the Outlet River and Sandbanks Provincial Park, whose beaches and freshwater dunes are on Lake Ontario; East Lake holds walleye, bass, sunfish and pike.  It rents boats, paddleboards, kayaks and canoes and has a playground, volleyball, horseshoes and a propane exchange.  It also rents cottages and log cabins and sells seasonal sites. --Claude

was: Small campground on a bend of the Saugeen River at 1343 Bruce County Rd 4, 3 km east of Walkerton. Operator site map colour-codes the inventory: a hydro+water block (49-61) and unserviced group sites (65, 66, 67) for overnight use, with the remaining ~50 numbered sites sold seasonal; overnight rates page posts hydro+water sites 54-61 at $75 CAD/night for two adults and unserviced group sites at $50. Dump station on site; also yurts, domes, bunkies and 4- and 6-person rental trailers, plus a tube run from the Maple Hill Dam. Open May 1 - Oct 18. Reservable online through Campspot. Overnight serviced inventory is small (roughly 8 sites), so book ahead. --Claude
note: Campground on the Saugeen River, a fly-fishing mecca, near Walkerton.  It rents kayaks, canoes and river tubes, and a free shuttle drops tubers at Maple Hill Dam for a float of about 1.5 to 2 hours back to camp; there are a children's fishing pond and free pedal carts.  Through the season there are 50/50 draws, potlucks, barbecues, fishing derbies, bingo, paint nights, the annual river run and weekend fly-fishing schools.  Outside firewood is not allowed; the campground provides local bundled wood.  The Lake Huron beaches at Port Elgin and Kincardine are a 30-minute drive.  It also rents bunkies, a Mongolian yurt, biodomes with hot tubs and saunas and a 3-bedroom trailer. --Claude

was: Family-run campground on the Serpent River off Hwy 17 midway between Sudbury and Sault Ste. Marie, about 1 km upstream of Lake Huron. Operator site map shows a mixed layout: transient loops A1-A6 and B1-B7 with 30-amp electric + water, transient 15-amp sites in the L row, and unserviced transient sites M1-M5/N1-N4, alongside a larger seasonal section (C-K rows) and 3 cabins. Directory listings give 78 sites total with 75 electric/water; no site sewer but a dump station on the way out. Pull-thru sites take large rigs. In-ground pool, store, laundry, boat launch, kayak rentals. Open May to mid-October; reservable online through Campspot. --Claude
note: Campground between Highway 17, the Trans-Canada, and the Serpent River, which empties into the North Shore of Lake Huron, midway between Sudbury and Sault Ste. Marie.  It has an inground pool, a playground, a private boat launch, a fishing pier, kayak rentals, a movie and book exchange and a pavilion, and hosts a weekly farmers market and food vendors through the week; a restaurant is across the street.  Its rustic log cabins are three on the river and two in the main campground, and boat and trailer storage is offered.  The office is open 7 days a week from May to mid-October, and check-in runs until 9 p.m. --Claude

was: Family campground at Greely, about 30 minutes south of Ottawa. Mostly seasonal lots but holds a real overnight block of roughly 30-40 transient sites, most with hookups; sites are back-in gravel and/or grass with a choice of 15- or 30-amp hydro plus water, and are long enough for larger trailers. Central washroom building with flush toilets and hot showers, pool, playground, mini-golf, themed weekends. Open early May to mid-October. Nightly sites are bookable online through Campspot; cabins also available. --Claude
note: Family campground in Greely, in the Ottawa area, whose sites have picnic tables and fire pits.  The pool has no lifeguard, and adult swim is from 3:30 to 4:30 p.m.; there are kids' play areas, horseshoes and an RC track, and Halloween is held over the Labour Day long weekend.  Long weekends take a 3-night minimum.  Outside firewood is not allowed, pets are limited to two per site, aggressive dogs such as Pit Bulls and Rottweilers are not permitted, and visitors pay $5 a day.  It also rents a bunky. --Claude

was: Private campground on Hwy 581 near Moonbeam, on two on-site lakes with sandy beaches and a water slide. Full-hookup and unserviced RV sites plus a seasonal section; 30-amp, water/electric, ~8 pull-thrus, big rigs to ~60 ft, dump station, showers/laundry. Reservable online (Campspot). --Claude
note: Campground of 252 lots near Moonbeam, 3 km in on Highway 581 from Highway 11, on spring-fed lakes up to 40 ft deep with sandy beaches and three small water slides for children.  A paving-stone path circles the lake, the lakes are good for swimming, pedal boats and kayaks, and there are three playgrounds and shuffleboard; fishing is free, and outboard motors are not allowed.  The chipstand is open daily from 11 a.m. to 8 p.m.  It also rents train apartments, a lofted bunkie and a deluxe cabin, and French is spoken. --Claude
